claims.text: The as-cast FeCoNiCrMn HEA has coarse grains.
Cold rolling followed by annealing can refine FeCoNiCrMn into an optimized nanograined microstructure.
Optimized grain boundaries minimize domain-wall pinning.
The refined microstructure accelerates spin-lattice thermal exchange.
Reduced domain-wall pinning and accelerated spin-lattice exchange enhance the magnetocaloric effect at low applied fields.
The proposed grain refinement preserves low magnetic hysteresis and mechanical stability.
The controlled intervention is 50% cold rolling followed by annealing at 750 °C for 30 minutes in an inert atmosphere.
Optimized grain boundaries can balance reduced domain-wall pinning against preservation of mechanical integrity.
Fine grains enhance exchange coupling across grain boundaries.
Reduced energetic barriers for domain-wall motion lower magnetic hysteresis.
Refined grain boundaries facilitate faster spin-lattice relaxation.
The grain-refined alloy will have a higher magnetic entropy change than the coarse-grained baseline at applied fields below 1 T.
The grain-refined alloy will exhibit less magnetic hysteresis than the coarse-grained baseline.
Grain-boundary reinforcement will maintain or enhance the alloy's mechanical strength.
The hypothesis is expected to apply below 1 T and approximately between 300 and 350 K.
Excessive grain refinement may produce magnetic inhomogeneity.
Excessive grain refinement may compromise mechanical properties.
A failure of increasing grain refinement to reduce hysteresis and increase magnetic entropy change would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis is bounded to optimized, non-excessive refinement and explicitly anticipates property deterioration after excessive refinement, yet the falsification rule treats deterioration caused by over-refinement as falsifying the hypothesis. An outcome outside the stated applicability boundary is not a decisive falsifier of the bounded hypothesis.
